messages.author: 900aa1be8773796a
messages.subject: Part 4 - error
parts:
Hi, 

Any assistance with how to address these errors would be much appreciated. 

Error in `[.data.frame`(S, , coln1 + ((i - 1) * 2)) :
  undefined columns selected
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In g.loadlog(params_sleep[["loglocation"]], coln1 = params_sleep[["coln1"]],  :
  NAs introduced by coercion
2:
None of the IDs in the accelerometer data could be matched with the ID numbers in the sleeplog. You may want to check that the ID format in your sleeplog is consistent with the ID column in the GGIR part2 csv-report, and that arguments coldid and sleeplogidnum are correctly set.

ps. the sleep log ID does match with the accelerometer data and NAs have been left blank in the sleep log. 

Cheers, 
Iyoma

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Part 4 - error
parts:
Thanks for posting this question Iyoma. Possibly there are trailing spaces in your IDs.
For example, your accelerometer file may have ID = "4567       ", while in Excel you may see it as "4567".

I recently addressed this for the activity log and I now realise that this may indeed also be a potential issue for the sleeplog.

I will add it to my to do list as this should be fairly easy to resolve and benefits many usecases.

In the mean-time you can can copy the ID extracted from the accelerometer file (part2 output) to the sleeplog to make them consistent, including trailing spaces file.

Cheers,

Vincent


Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

messages.author: aabdecdc2eb3d744
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Part 4 - error
parts:
Hi Vincent,

Thanks for your reply. Attached you will find the requested documents. In the meantime, the problem has solved itself partially. I encounter the problem only while running GGIR on a computing server (Digital Research Environment, DRE). Here, the problem persists. However, when I download the output of parts 1-3 and run parts 4 and 5 from my local C:/ drive, the problem does not occur. I've tried several combinations regarding the sleeplog: a sleeplog with a single participant, or a sleep log with multiple participants for batch analysis; a simple sleeplog without nap times, or an advanced sleeplog with nap times. The error only occurs in the DRE and not on my local computer. The problem is pretty much irrelevant for me, as I only need the cloud computer for part 1; running parts 2-5 from my local computer is fine. But maybe this problem is worth looking into for other users...

Regarding my other post about activPAL, no news since my latest reply on 15 February. The auto-calibration function seems to cause the error, but after bypassing this by setting "do.cal = FALSE", the GGIR function works fine. So auto-calibration currently seems to be an issue for activPAL data. To limit the potential bias this introduces, I'm now using the MAD metric instead of ENMO.

Best, Koen

parts:
Hi Koen,

In your R script I see:

 sleeplogsep = ","

but when I open your sleeplog in notepad I see all columns separated by a ";"
Can you try changing it to sleeplogsep = ";" ?

I am wondering whether your local computer may be better able to handle this variation  in column separator than your digital research environment?

Best, Vincent
